note: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Countries & Cultures page. Per country: id, en/ar names, flag (emoji), demonym_en, demonym_ar_m/f, capital_en/ar, region, population (approximate, editable), muslim_pct (approximate %, drives the breakdown bar), breakdown (free-text notes on peoples/communities), languages[], bbox [west,south,east,north] for the map view, facts (free text), vocab_theme (theme number on the Arabic vocab page for the matching 'I am …' phrases), and status ('ok' | 'placeholder'). Figures are rounded classroom approximations — refine freely. Add countries by appending; the page sorts by array order.

countries.breakdown: Arabs and Kurds are the largest peoples, with Turkmen, Assyrian/Chaldean Christians, Yazidis, and Mandaeans among its historic communities. Home to the shrine cities of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra.
countries.facts: The land of Mesopotamia — the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, ancient Babylon, and centuries of Islamic scholarship in Baghdad, Najaf, and Karbala.

countries.breakdown: A famously diverse country: Shia and Sunni Muslims, Maronite and Orthodox Christians, Druze, and more, living among mountains and the Mediterranean coast.
countries.facts: Known for its cedar trees (on the flag), the ancient Phoenician ports, and a rich food and literary culture.

countries.breakdown: Arab majority with large expatriate communities from across Asia and Africa. Home of Makkah and Madinah — the destination of Hajj for the whole Muslim world.
countries.facts: The birthplace of the Prophet ﷺ and of revelation — the Ka'bah in Makkah is the qiblah of every prayer.

countries.breakdown: The Arab world's most populous country — Muslim majority with the large Coptic Christian community among its oldest peoples.
countries.facts: The Nile, the pyramids, and al-Azhar in Cairo — a center of Arabic and Islamic learning for over a thousand years. Mentioned by name in the Quran.

countries.breakdown: Turks form the majority alongside a large Kurdish population; Istanbul spans two continents across the Bosphorus.
countries.facts: Heir to the Ottoman capital Istanbul, with masterpiece mosques like the Süleymaniye and the Blue Mosque.

countries.breakdown: Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashtun, Baloch, and Muhajir peoples among others — one of the largest Muslim populations in the world.
countries.facts: From the peaks of the Karakoram to the Indus valley — founded in 1947 as a homeland for the Muslims of South Asia.

countries.breakdown: The world's largest Muslim population, spread across 17,000+ islands — Javanese and Sundanese are the biggest of its hundreds of peoples.
countries.facts: Islam arrived by trade and spread by character and da'wah — today more Muslims live here than in any other country.
